checked.found: Memphis decree of 27 March 196 BC in Egyptian hieroglyphic, Demotic and Greek; the king remitted taxes and crown debts. Name accurate.
Census of 2 CE, about 12.2 million households and 59.6 million people; the earliest census with preserved records (Britannica, historyofinformation).
Tax census of the newly created province of Judea in 6 CE, ordered of Quirinius; Luke links it to Jesus's birth.

Year 991 confirmed: 10,000 pounds of silver paid after Maldon. The claim that the king 'then taxed his people to raise it' rests only on a popular-history site; Wikipedia dates the national land tax to 1012 and I found no scholarly source for a 991 levy.
checked.suggestion: Consider dropping 'then taxed his people to raise it', for example: 'After a defeat by Viking raiders, an English king handed over a huge sum of silver to buy peace.'

checked.found: 1188 levy of 10% on revenues and movables, prompted by Saladin's capture of Jerusalem, to fund the Third Crusade (ordinance covered England and France).
First writs 1634 to coastal counties in peacetime during the Personal Rule, extended to inland counties in 1635.
Introduced 1696 (repealed 1851); owners bricked up windows to get under thresholds.

Beard tax imposed 5 September 1698; linked to Westernisation, nobles and officials charged, token issued as proof of payment. One source disputes the motive but the description's claim is the mainstream account.
Importation Act 1815 (royal assent 23 March 1815) barred foreign grain until domestic wheat reached 80 shillings a quarter.
1842 budget under Conservative PM Peel revived income tax in peacetime to fund tariff cuts on hundreds of articles; the tax has continued since.

Year 1861 confirmed (Revenue Act signed 5 August 1861, 3% on incomes over $800, Civil War funding). But sources say the 1861 tax was repealed and replaced within a year by the Revenue Act of 1862, not 'let lapse'; the income tax as a whole expired in 1872, so the wording is ambiguous.
checked.suggestion: Consider 'To fund a civil war, Congress taxed incomes for the first time, then replaced the measure the next year.'

checked.found: Introduced 29 April 1909 by Chancellor Lloyd George; land taxes and higher taxes on the rich to fund pensions and naval building; Lords rejected it in November 1909.
Current Tax Payment Act of 1943 required employers to withhold federal income tax from wages, starting 1 July 1943.
Law of 10 April 1954, devised by Maurice Laure, taxing value added at each stage; initially large firms; later spread worldwide.
Passed 6 June 1978; capped property tax at 1% of assessed value, required two-thirds legislative vote for state tax increases; sparked a national tax revolt.
Community charge began in Scotland April 1989, a year before England and Wales; mass non-payment in Scotland; riots in London March 1990.
Tariff cuts began 1 January 1994, with most duties phased out over 5 to 15 years among the US, Canada and Mexico.
Agricultural tax abolished effective 1 January 2006 by NPC Standing Committee resolution; described as ancient or long-standing.
8 October 2021: 136 countries agreed to a 15% minimum corporate tax rate to curb profit shifting.
